Playbook (accumulated from past tasks):
## strategies
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When adding a money-computing function, check existing sibling functions (e.g. line_total, invoice_total) for the project's rounding/helper conventions and mirror them, including wrapping the final result in round_money.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Passing visible tests is not sufficient for money functions: verify rounding convention compliance explicitly, since hidden tests check half-up rounding that default Decimal division/round() will fail.
## domain_facts
[ace-0001] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: In ledgerly, money values must be rounded with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.

item.content: When validating an integer parameter, reject bool explicitly (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since bool is a subclass of int and True/False would otherwise pass as 1/0.

Mirror existing error codes and message formats from sibling functions (e.g. invalid_state with f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}") so new validation paths stay consistent with the codebase's BillingError conventions.

Don't assume a numeric input is already Decimal; coerce with to_money() before round_money() and comparisons, since callers may pass int, str, or float and raw comparisons/rounding will fail or misbehave.
